cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet gets another word from the LORD, and friend, there's no small talk in this one. God calls him son of man and asks him a question. Will he pass judgment on the city of bloodshed?

cards.question: God asks Ezekiel if he'll pass judgment on the city of bloodshed. Then what does God tell him to do with her?

answers.text: Confront her with all her abominations
Comfort her in all her troubles
Remind her of all her victories

cards.text: Here's what the Lord GOD says to the city. She's bringing her own doom on herself, friend, and two things are doing it.

cards.question: The city brings her own doom by shedding blood within her walls and making ___ to defile herself.

cards.text: God says she's guilty of the blood she's shed, and she's brought her days to a close. Now the other nations are watching.

cards.question: God says the city's days are at an end. How will the lands near and far treat her?

cards.text: God calls her an infamous city, full of turmoil, mocked near AND far. Friend, that's not one group chat laughing at you. That's EVERY group chat.
Then God gets specific: every prince of Israel in her has used his power to shed blood.

cards.question: Inside the city of bloodshed, father and mother are treated with honor. True or false?
Within the city's walls, the foreign resident is exploited. Who else is oppressed there?
The city has despised God's holy things and ___ His Sabbaths.

cards.text: The list keeps going: slanderous men bent on bloodshed, and people who eat on the mountain shrines and commit acts of indecency.

In her, men uncover the nakedness of their fathers and violate women during their menstrual impurity. One man commits an abomination with his neighbor's wife, another wickedly defiles his daughter-in-law, and another violates his own sister.
Then the money comes in: usury, excess interest, extorting the neighbors. Friend, this city would charge you a fee just for asking about the fees.

cards.question: The people of the city take bribes to shed blood and extort their neighbors. Then God says one more thing: they have ___ Him.

cards.text: Now God strikes His hands together against her unjust gain and the blood shed in her midst. Then He asks if her courage will endure on the day He deals with her.

cards.question: God tells the city that He, the LORD, has spoken, and He will act. True or false?
Now God tells the city what's coming. What will He do with her people?

answers.text: Hide them up in the mountains
Send them all back to Egypt

cards.question: God says He'll purge the city's uncleanness. When she has defiled herself in the eyes of the nations, what does God say she will know?

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again. God says the house of Israel has become dross to Him, all copper, tin, iron and lead inside the furnace.

cards.question: Because the house of Israel has become dross, God says He'll gather them into one city. Which one?

cards.text: Then God gives a picture from the furnace. Just as metal gets gathered into it, that's how He'll gather the house of Israel, in His anger and wrath.

cards.question: God says once the house of Israel is gathered, He'll leave them there and melt them. True or false?

cards.text: Then God says it again: He'll blow on the house of Israel with the fire of His wrath and melt them within the city. Then they'll know the LORD has poured out His wrath on them.
Another word from the LORD comes to Ezekiel, with a message to say to her. She's a land, and in the day of indignation, no rain has fallen on her.

cards.question: In the day of indignation, the land that no rain has fallen on is a land that has not been ___.

cards.text: Now God goes down the list of who's in charge, starting with the princes. Their conspiracy is like a roaring lion tearing its prey.

cards.question: The princes devour the people and seize the treasures and precious things. What do they multiply within the land?
Next God turns to the priests. They do violence to His law and make no distinction between the holy and the ___.

cards.text: Then come the officials, and they're no better. They're like wolves tearing their prey, destroying lives for dishonest gain.

cards.question: The princes, the priests and the officials are all doing harm. What do the land's prophets do with these deeds?

answers.text: Hide away from them in the hills

cards.text: The prophets even say, “This is what the Lord GOD says,” when the LORD has not spoken.

cards.question: With leaders like this, at least the everyday people of the land treat the poor and needy fairly. True or false?
God says He searched for a man to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Him on behalf of the land, so that He should not destroy it. How many did He find?

cards.text: So God says He has poured out His indignation on them and brought their ways down on their own heads. Heavy word, friend, and you stayed with it all the way to the end.
